messages.author: a860e462befdcbf7
messages.subject: High-level predictors
parts:
Hi All,

I have what I think is a simple question. I have a two level Negative Binomial regression and I want to include high-level predictors. What is the appropriate way of doing this? Importantly, how do I specify effects on the intercepts and on the slopes?

As a simple illustration, I have i data points in k groups:

y[ik] ~ a0[k] + b0[k]*x[ik]
a0[k] ~ N(a1 + b1*P[k])
b0[k] ~ N(a2 + b2*P[k])

Where P[k] are the high-level predictors.

Any help would be much appreciated,

thanks,

Ignacio

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: High-level predictors
parts:
Dear Ignacio,

By considering the indexes sets
id0 <- id1 <- 1:n
and the formula
a0 + f(id0, model='iid') +
x + f(id1, x, model='iid')
implements the model
a0 + b0*x + a_i + b_i * x_i
for
a_{1...n} ~ N(0, sigma1^2 * I)
b_{1...n} ~ N(0, sigma1^2 * I)
and you can allow non iid Gaussian distribution by choosing one of the
models in
names(inla.models()$latent)

Elias
